s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic musculoskeletal pain and stress fractures with abnormal bone mineralization
salient_findings: Stress fractures of the left rib, left sacrum, and left femoral neck
Abnormal bone densitometry with Z-scores of −2.5 in the lumbar spine and −1.9 in the femoral neck
key_facts: 2-year history of hip pain following low-impact falls
Elevated alkaline phosphatase level of 220 U/L
Bone densitometry showed Z-scores of −2.5 in the lumbar spine and −1.9 in the femoral neck
Genetic evaluation for hypophosphatemic disorders was unremarkable
Family history was negative for bone disease

shortlist.label: Tumor-induced osteomalacia
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated FGF23 level and presence of an intracortical lesion on gallium-68 DOTATATE PET/MRI

shortlist.label: Hypophosphatasia
shortlist.why_kept: Low phosphorus level and elevated alkaline phosphatase level

shortlist.label: Osteomalacia
shortlist.why_kept: Low 25-OH vitamin D level and low phosphorus level

shortlist.label: X-linked hypophosphatemia
shortlist.why_kept: Low phosphorus level and family history of bone disease, although genetic evaluation was unremarkable

shortlist.label: Fibrous dysplasia
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of stress fractures and abnormal bone mineralization

raw.rationale: The patient's elevated FGF23 level, low phosphorus level, and presence of an intracortical lesion on the gallium-68 DOTATATE PET/MRI are consistent with tumor-induced osteomalacia

rejected.label: Hypophosphatasia
rejected.why: Genetic evaluation was unremarkable and alkaline phosphatase was elevated, which is not typical for hypophosphatasia

rejected.label: Osteomalacia
rejected.why: While the patient has low phosphorus and vitamin D levels, the presence of a tumor and elevated FGF23 suggests a more specific diagnosis

rejected.label: X-linked hypophosphatemia
rejected.why: Genetic evaluation was unremarkable and family history was negative for bone disease

rejected.label: Fibrous dysplasia
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings are not typical for fibrous dysplasia, and the presence of a tumor and elevated FGF23 suggests a different diagnosis
